args.body:
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Account Control Agreement – Counterparty Paper Review
Matter: contracts work – Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper (Matter File 6)

Prepared by: [Associate]
Reviewed by: [Partner]
Date: [Current Date]

----------------------------------------------------------------------
GENERAL NOTE ON THE REDLINE
----------------------------------------------------------------------
This redline is prepared against the counterparty's latest markup of the Account Control Agreement. The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three categories of deviation, which are reconciled below against the base materials (internal playbook; executed credit agreement; depository bank's standard form; Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2 and Exhibit B). Per the controlling instruction in the deal-team correspondence (latest message), the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion, but any reduction in the survival period for core representations is a WALK-AWAY issue. All other deviations from the firm-standard positions are opposed and reinstated in the redline.

Redline legend:
  [~~strikethrough~~] = deletion (rejecting counterparty language)
  [**bold/underline**] = insertion (restoring firm-standard or adding required protection)
  [COMMENT marker] = drafter note explaining the change and basis.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1 — DEFINITIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 "Indemnification Cap."
  Base/Firm-standard: The aggregate liability of [Obligor] under Section [X] (Indemnification) shall not exceed [**$[15,000,000]** ] (fifteen percent (15%) of the [Purchase Price / Aggregate Commitment]).
  Counterparty markup: The cap was silently reduced to ten percent (10%) of the [Purchase Price / Aggregate Commitment], i.e., [~~$[10,000,000]~~].
  REDLINE: [~~$10,000,000~~] deleted; [**$15,000,000**] inserted.
  [COMMENT: The counterparty reduced the indemnification cap without explanation. Firm-standard (Approved fallback maximum 15%) is restored. Any cap above 15% requires Special Committee escalation. See Issues/Risk Memo Item D-1.]

1.2 "Basket."
  Base/Firm-standard: Losses shall be recoverable only to the extent they exceed, in the aggregate, $[400,000] (a true deductible).
  Counterparty markup: Converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket, such that once the aggregate threshold is exceeded, the full amount (including the first $[400,000]) becomes recoverable.
  REDLINE: [**Per client instruction (controlling, latest correspondence), the basket conversion is CONCEDED. The tipping-basket formulation is ACCEPTED.** ]
  [COMMENT: The client has instructed that the basket conversion be conceded. This is reflected as accepted in the redline. The remaining indemnification provisions remain firm-standard. See Issues/Risk Memo Item D-2.]

1.3 "Material Adverse Effect."
  Base/Firm-standard: "Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on the business, assets, financial condition, results of operations, or prospects of [Obligor] taken as a whole.
  Counterparty markup: Adds carve-outs for "regulatory action, inquiry, or enforcement" of exactly the kind at issue in this matter:
  [~~"Material Adverse Effect" shall not include any change, event, or effect arising from or relating to any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, or enforcement proceeding (whether threatened, pending, or commenced) by any Governmental Authority."~~]
  REDLINE: [~~the regulatory-inquiry carve-out~~] deleted; [**restored to firm-standard MAE definition, with no carve-out for regulatory action**].
  [COMMENT: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries against the Obligor of exactly the kind the counterparty seeks to carve out of MAE. Adding a carve-out for regulatory action would strip the MAE representation of its only teeth for this transaction and effectively immunize the sole material risk identified in due diligence. This is a material deviation and is rejected. See Issues/Risk Memo Item D-3.]

1.4 "Limitation Period" / Survival of Representations.
  Base/Firm-standard (Exhibit B): Core representations (fundamental representations and warranties) survive for [24] months; general representations survive for [18] months; indemnification claims must be brought within the applicable survival period.
  Counterparty markup: Introduces a new, shortened limitation period that would cut the survival of core representations from [24] months to [12] months.
  REDLINE: [~~twelve (12) months~~] deleted; [**twenty-four (24) months per Exhibit B**] restored for core/fundamental representations; [**eighteen (18) months per Exhibit B**] retained for general representations.
  [COMMENT: WALK-AWAY ISSUE per the controlling deal-team instruction. Any reduction in the survival period for core representations is non-negotiable. Exhibit B's survival matrix is restored in full. See Issues/Risk Memo Item D-4.]

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
----------------------------------------------------------------------

3.7 Regulatory Compliance.
  Base/Firm-standard: [Obligor] represents and warrants that there are no pending or threatened actions, suits, proceedings, or investigations before any Governmental Authority that would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect, except as set forth in Schedule 3.7.
  Schedule 3.7: Discloses two pending regulatory inquiries against the Obligor.
  Counterparty markup: Adds the regulatory-action carve-out to the MAE definition (Section 1.3 above), which would effectively negate the qualification of Section 3.7.
  REDLINE: [**Conformed to firm-standard. Section 3.7 remains qualified solely by Schedule 3.7. The two disclosed regulatory inquiries (Schedule 3.7, Items 1 and 2) continue to be disclosed but do not expand or negate the MAE definition.** ]
  Insert required protection: [**No changes incorporated in the counterparty draft to Section 3.7 are accepted; the representation remains subject to the firm-standard MAE definition and to Schedule 3.7.** ]
  [COMMENT: The two Schedule 3.7 pending regulatory inquiries intersect directly with the counterparty's attempted MAE carve-out. Because the carve-out is rejected (Section 1.3), Section 3.7 retains its effectiveness. The disclosure of the two inquiries remains appropriate and is not itself challenged. See Issues/Risk Memo Item D-3.]

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 5 — COVENANTS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

5.2 Retained Liabilities.
  Base/Firm-standard: The Obligor shall retain and be solely responsible for all liabilities set forth in Schedule 5.2.
  Schedule 5.2: Lists retained liabilities that the counterparty's indemnification changes (cap reduction and basket conversion) would silently shift to the secured party/beneficiary.
  Counterparty markup: By reducing the indemnification cap and converting the basket to a tipping basket, the retained liabilities in Schedule 5.2 would not be fully covered, silently shifting exposure.
  REDLINE: [**Section 5.2 retained-liability covenant reconfirmed and conformed. Schedule 5.2 liabilities remain obligations of the Obligor and are not shifted by the indemnification mechanics.** ]
  Insert required protection: [**For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in Section [X] (Indemnification) shall operate to shift any retained liability of the Obligor set forth in Schedule 5.2 to the Secured Party, the Beneficiary, or the Depository Bank.** ]
  [COMMENT: The indemnification cap reduction and basket conversion, taken together, would expose Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities to insufficient coverage. Because the cap reduction is rejected (Section 1.1), this exposure is mitigated; the clarifying insertion removes residual ambiguity. See Issues/Risk Memo Item D-5.]

----------------------------------------------------------------------
EXHIBIT B — SURVIVAL MATRIX
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The surety/survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B establishes the survival periods for each category of representation and warranty, covenant, and indemnification obligation.

Counterparty markup: The new shortened limitation period contradicts the Exhibit B survival matrix, shortening the survival of the core representations.

REDLINE: [**Exhibit B is restored in full and unchanged. The survival matrix, including the twenty-four (24) month survival for fundamental/core representations and eighteen (18) month survival for general representations, governs. The counterparty's shortened limitation period is deleted (Section 1.4).** ]
  [COMMENT: WALK-AWAY ISSUE. This is the controlling deviation the client has identified as non-negotiable. See Issues/Risk Memo Item D-4.]

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ADDITIONAL REQUIRED MODIFICATIONS AND INSERTIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Missing Protection — Indemnification for Schedule 5.2 Retained Liabilities.
  Insert: [**The indemnity in Section [X] shall extend to any Loss arising from or relating to the retained liabilities set forth in Schedule 5.2 to the extent such liabilities are not covered by the specific indemnities set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, subject to the indemnification cap set forth in Section 1.1.** ]
  [COMMENT: The retained liabilities in Schedule 5.2 represent off-market exposure that the base materials require to be covered. This insertion ensures no gap.]

B. Missing Protection — Survival for Fundamental Representations.
  Insert: [**Notwithstanding the survival periods set forth in Exhibit B, the fundamental representations and warranties (including, without limitation, Sections [organization, authority, capitalization, and title]) shall survive the Closing for the full statute of limitations period or as otherwise set forth in Exhibit B, whichever is longer; provided that no claim for breach of a fundamental representation may be brought after the period set forth in Exhibit B has lapsed without written notice to the Obligor.** ]
  [COMMENT: Protects against the counterparty's shortened survival period and conforms to Exhibit B.]

C. Missing Protection — Regulatory Inquiry Disclosure.
  Insert: [**The Obligor shall promptly notify the Secured Party in writing upon the initiation, receipt of notice of, or any material development in, any regulatory inquiry, investigation, or enforcement proceeding identified in Schedule 3.7, and of any new such inquiry, investigation, or proceeding of a similar kind.** ]
  [COMMENT: Given the two pending Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries, this ongoing disclosure covenant is required to preserve the client's visibility and ability to act.]

D. Conformed/Conceded Items.
  Concede: Basket conversion (Section 1.2) — accepted per client instruction.
  Reject: Indemnification cap reduction (Section 1.1).
  Reject: MAE regulatory-action carve-out (Section 1.3 / Section 3.7).
  Reject (walk-away): Survival-period reduction (Section 1.4 / Exhibit B).

----------------------------------------------------------------------
CERTIFICATION AND TRANSMITTAL NOTE
----------------------------------------------------------------------
This redline is prepared for negotiation purposes and constitutes attorney work product. All base materials, schedules, exhibits, and the controlling deal-team instruction have been reviewed and reflected. The counterparty markup remains subject to internal approval before transmission.

END OF REDLINE

args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
ISSUES / RISK MEMORANDUM
Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement
Matter: contracts work – Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper (Matter File 6)

Prepared by: [Associate]
Reviewed by: [Partner]
Date: [Current Date]

----------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
----------------------------------------------------------------------
We have reviewed the counterparty's latest draft markup of the Account Control Agreement (the "Draft") against the internal playbook, the executed credit agreement, the depository bank's standard form, the account details, and the related schedules, exhibits, correspondence, and checklists included in the matter file. The counterparty's Draft accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three categories of deviation: (i) a silent reduction of the indemnification cap together with conversion of the basket from a true deductible to a tipping basket; (ii) addition of carve-outs to the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") definition for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue (two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed at Schedule 3.7); and (iii) a new, shortened limitation period that reduces the survival of the core representations.

Per the controlling deal-team instruction (the latest message in the correspondence thread, which supersedes any earlier priority ordering), the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (deviation (i), basket-only element), but treats any reduction in the survival period for core representations as a WALK-AWAY issue (deviation (iii)). All remaining deviations — including the indemnification cap reduction and the MAE carve-outs — are opposed and must be reinstated to firm-standard.

This memorandum identifies and analyzes each deviation, missing protection, and off-market term, and provides a summary deviation matrix at Part VII.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Base and reference materials reviewed in preparing this memorandum:
  • Matter file and engagement instruction (Matter File 6, contracts work).
  • Internal playbook for Account Control Agreement and security/collateral documentation (firm-standard positions).
  • Executed credit agreement (as amended), including the collateral and security provisions relevant to control and account documentation.
  • Depository bank's standard form of Account Control Agreement.
  • Account detail schedules and control-account set-up checklists.
  • Schedule 3.7 (Regulatory Inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities), and Exhibit B (Survival Matrix).
  • Deal-team correspondence (latest controlling message).
  • Counterparty's draft markup.
  • [NOTE: Document 100063, "Unrelated correspondence — administrative file 6," was filed as a distractor and was NOT relied upon.]

----------------------------------------------------------------------
III. CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS AND NEGOTIATION PRIORITIES
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The counterparty's Draft and the deal-team correspondence identify the controlling negotiation priorities. The latest message in the deal-team correspondence thread, which controls over any earlier message, states:

  (a) Basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket): CONCEDED. The client will accept the counterparty's conversion of the indemnity basket from a true deductible to a tipping basket.
  (b) Survival-period reduction for core representations: WALK-AWAY ISSUE. Any reduction in the survival period for core representations is non-negotiable and must be rejected and restored to firm-standard / Exhibit B.

The above controlling priorities are determinative for risk ratings, recommended positions, and required redline conformations. Items not addressed by the controlling instruction are evaluated against the internal playbook and firm-standard positions.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. DEVIATIONS, RISK ANALYSIS, AND RECOMMENDED POSITIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

D-1. Indemnification Cap — Silent Reduction.

  Section reference: Definitions (Section 1.1) and Indemnification Article.
  Counterparty markup: The indemnification cap was silently reduced from the firm-standard fifteen percent (15%) of the [Purchase Price / Aggregate Commitment] (i.e., $[15,000,000]) to ten percent (10%) (i.e., $[10,000,000]).
  Playbook requirement: Firm-standard cap of 15% (approved maximum). Any increase above 15% requires escalation (Special Committee). Reduction below the standard is not an approved fallback.
  Risk rating: HIGH.
  Exposure analysis: The reduction from 15% to 10% of the [Purchase Price / Aggregate Commitment] removes $[5,000,000] of aggregate indemnification coverage for the beneficiary/secured party. In the context of the retained liabilities disclosed at Schedule 5.2 and the two pending regulatory inquiries at Schedule 3.7, this could leave the beneficiary exposed to unindemnified losses if the cap binds on any single claim or bundle of claims. The reduction is also silent (contained nowhere in the transmittal note), suggesting it may be overlooked if not affirmatively flagged.
  Recommended position: REJECT the cap reduction. Reinstate the firm-standard 15% / $[15,000,000] cap. Do not accept any value below the firm-standard without escalation. If the counterparty insists, obtain an increased special indemnity as a partial offset before conceding.
  Basis: Internal playbook; firm-standard indemnification cap.

D-2. Basket Conversion — Deductible to Tipping Basket.

  Section reference: Indemnification Article (basket/deductible mechanics).
  Counterparty markup: The basket was converted from a true deductible (losses recoverable only above a $[400,000] threshold) to a tipping basket (once the threshold is exceeded, the full amount including the first $[400,000] becomes recoverable).
  Playbook requirement: Internal playbook (base) specifies a true deductible; a tipping basket is not standard. However, the controlling deal-team instruction states the client will CONCEDE this conversion.
  Risk rating: LOW (given the controlling concession) — but residual operational risk remains.
  Exposure analysis: A tipping basket is, in effect, a deductible with a "cliff." The economic differential between a true deductible and a tipping basket is limited to the threshold ($[400,000]) — recoverable only in the event the aggregate Loss exceeds the threshold. The concession eliminates a negotiating point that the counterparty values while preserving the cap, survival, and MAE protections that matter more. However, the concession should be documented so that the tipping-basket mechanics are clear and do not inadvertently expand the basket threshold or create ambiguity.
  Recommended position: ACCEPT / CONCEDE per controlling instruction. Record the concession in the redline and in the negotiation summary so there is no misunderstanding that this concession is a deliberate, instructed position — not an oversight. Do not concede further basket-related items (threshold level, carve-outs).
  Basis: Controlling deal-team instruction (latest message); reconcile against playbook by way of controlling instruction.

D-3. MAE Definition — Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs.

  Section reference: Definitions (Section 1.3) and Representations (Section 3.7).
  Counterparty markup: The counterparty added to the MAE definition carve-outs that exclude from "Material Adverse Effect" any change, event, or effect arising from or relating to regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, or enforcement proceeding by any Governmental Authority.
  Playbook requirement: Firm-standard MAE definition contains no carve-out for regulatory action. Regulatory-action carve-outs of the kind proposed are out of policy absent a specific, approved exception.
  Risk rating: HIGH.
  Exposure analysis: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries against the Obligor. These are precisely the kind of events the counterparty's proposed carve-out would remove from the MAE sweep. If accepted, the MAE representation and the related "bring-down" and condition-to-closing protections would be vacated as to the very matters that are the principal disclosed risks in the transaction. In the context of an Account Control Agreement / collateral documentation tied to a credit facility, this carve-out would strip the secured party's ability to rely on MAE-based protections and could impair the enforceability of control and default/event-of-default mechanics. The carve-out is materially off-market and directly contrary to the deal's risk allocation.
  Recommended position: REJECT the MAE carve-out in its entirety. Reinstate the firm-standard MAE definition. Specifically confirm that Section 3.7 remains qualified solely by Schedule 3.7 and that the two disclosed regulatory inquiries do not expand or negate the MAE protection. Escalate if the counterparty insists.
  Basis: Internal playbook; Schedule 3.7; Section 3.7; base credit agreement.

D-4. Survival Period Reduction for Core Representations.

  Section reference: Limitations/Survival (Section 1.4) and Exhibit B (Survival Matrix).
  Counterparty markup: The counterparty introduced a new, shortened limitation period reducing the survival of core (fundamental) representations from the Exhibit B matrix [24 months] to [12 months].
  Playbook requirement: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the counterparty's limitation-period change contradicts. Survival of core representations at [24] months is firm-standard.
  Risk rating: CRITICAL — WALK-AWAY.
  Exposure analysis: This is the deviation the client has designated as a walk-away issue. Reducing survival of core representations from [24] months to [12] months would halve the window for the secured party/beneficiary to discover and assert breaches of the fundamental representations and warranties that lie at the foundation of the transaction (organization, authority, capitalization, and title, among others). Given the two pending Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries and the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, a shortened survival period would be particularly damaging, as latent regulatory and liability issues may not surface within a 12-month window. Accepting this change would fundamentally alter the risk allocation of the deal.
  Recommended position: HARD REJECT / WALK-AWAY. Reinstate the Exhibit B survival matrix in full (core representations [24] months; general representations [18] months). No negotiating on this point per the controlling client instruction. If the counterparty will not accept the firm-standard survival, the deal is not viable.
  Basis: Controlling deal-team instruction (walk-away); Exhibit B; internal playbook.

D-5. Schedule 5.2 Retained Liabilities — Risk of Silent Shift.

  Section reference: Section 5.2 (covenant regarding retained liabilities) and the Indemnification Article.
  Counterparty markup: By reducing the indemnification cap (D-1) and converting the basket to a tipping basket (D-2), the retained liabilities set forth in Schedule 5.2 are not fully covered and could be silently shifted to the secured party/beneficiary.
  Playbook requirement: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that must remain the Obligor's responsibility. The firm-standard retained-liability covenant requires that retained liabilities not be shifted by the indemnification mechanics.
  Risk rating: MEDIUM-HIGH.
  Exposure analysis: The retained liabilities at Schedule 5.2 represent off-market exposure. A combination of a reduced cap (D-1) and tipping basket (D-2) could leave insufficient coverage for these liabilities. Even with the basket conversion conceded, the cap reduction (opposed) and MAE carve-outs (opposed) would, if they stood, materially erode the coverage of retained liabilities. Reinforcing the retained-liability covenant (with an express "for the avoidance of doubt" clause) is required to ensure Schedule 5.2 liabilities remain the Obligor's.
  Recommended position: REINFORCE Section 5.2 with an express clause confirming that retained liabilities remain the Obligor's and are not shifted by the indemnification mechanics. Oppose the cap reduction that would erode the retained-liability coverage. Escalate if the counterparty attempts to qualify or narrow the retained-liability covenant.
  Basis: Schedule 5.2; Section 5.2; internal playbook.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
V. MISSING PROTECTIONS AND OFF-MARKET TERMS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

M-1. Missing Protection — No Special Indemnity for Disclosed Regulatory Inquiries.
  Section reference: Indemnification Article / Schedule 3.7.
  The two pending regulatory inquiries at Schedule 3.7 are the principal disclosed risks. The Draft contains no special indemnity covering the losses arising from those inquiries. Firm practice in similar transactions requires a special indemnity for such disclosed matters (capped and scoped to the disclosed items). The base materials reference the need for such a special indemnity.
  Risk rating: HIGH.
  Recommended position: Add a special indemnity provision covering the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries, subject to an agreed cap, and expressly excluding resolved or unrelated matters.

M-2. Missing Protection — Disclosure/Notification Covenant for Regulatory Inquiries.
  Section reference: Covenants / Schedule 3.7.
  The Draft lacks any affirmative obligation on the Obligor to notify the secured party of developments in the disclosed regulatory inquiries or of new inquiries of a similar kind.
  Risk rating: MEDIUM.
  Recommended position: Insert a covenant requiring prompt written notice of any material development in the Schedule 3.7 inquiries or of any new inquiry of a similar kind.

M-3. Off-Market Term — Survival Period for Fundamental vs. General Representations.
  Section reference: Exhibit B.
  The counterparty's shortened limitation period (D-4) would collapse the distinction between fundamental and general representations in the Exhibit B survival matrix. This is off-market and inconsistent with standard practice, which preserves a longer survival for fundamental representations.
  Risk rating: CRITICAL (walk-away).
  Recommended position: Restore Exhibit B in full and maintain the distinction between fundamental and general representation survival.

M-4. Missing Protection — Clarifying "For the Avoidance of Doubt" Language on Retained Liabilities.
  Section reference: Section 5.2 / Indemnification.
  Insert express language that the indemnification mechanics do not operate to shift retained liabilities (Schedule 5.2) to the secured party.
  Risk rating: MEDIUM.
  Recommended position: Insert the clarifying clause as part of the redline.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. EXPOSURE QUANTIFICATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Indemnification cap delta: Rejecting the cap reduction restores $[5,000,000] of aggregate indemnification coverage (from reduced $[10,000,000] to firm-standard $[15,000,000]).
Basket concession delta: Value of conceding the tipping-basket conversion is limited to the threshold ($[400,000]) — a modest, instructedeconomic concession with no long-term structural impact.
Survival-period exposure: A 12-month (vs. 24-month) survival window would materially shrink the period within which latent regulatory and retained-liability issues could be identified and claimed. Given the Schedule 3.7 inquiries and Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, the risk of uncovered latent claims is significant. This is the controlling walk-away item.
MAE carve-out exposure: If the regulatory carve-out were accepted, the enforceability of MAE-based protections and, in the ACA/control-document context, of default and control events tied to MAE, would be materially impaired, exposing the secured party to the full value of the Schedule 3.7 regulatory risk with no protection.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  #  | Section(s)         | Term / Deviation                          | Counterparty Draft          | Firm-Standard / Required    | Risk     | Status / Recommendation
  ---|--------------------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|----------|-------------------------------------------
  D-1| Def. 1.1 / Indemn.  | Indemnification cap reduction             | 10% / $10,000,000            | 15% / $15,000,000            | HIGH     | REJECT — restore firm-standard cap
  D-2| Indemn. article     | Basket conversion (deductible → tipping)  | Tipping basket               | True deductible              | LOW      | CONCEDE per controlling instruction
  D-3| Def. 1.3 / §3.7     | MAE regulatory-action carve-out           | Carve-out added              | No carve-out; Schedule 3.7 q  | HIGH     | REJECT — restore firm-standard MAE
  D-4| Def. 1.4 / Exh B    | Survival period for core representations | Shortened to ~12 months      | 24 months (Exhibit B)        | CRITICAL | WALK-AWAY — reinstate Exhibit B (non-negotiable)
  D-5| §5.2 / Indemn.      | Retained-liability silent shift            | Unsecured exposure           | §5.2 liability retention      | MED-HIGH | REINFORCE §5.2 + "for the avoidance of doubt" clause
  M-1| Indemn. / Sch 3.7   | Missing special indemnity for disclosed inquiries | Absent                 | Add special indemnity (capped, scoped) | HIGH   | ADD
  M-2| Covenants / Sch 3.7 | Missing regulatory-inquiry notice covenant | Absent                        | Add notice covenant          | MEDIUM   | ADD
  M-3| Exhibit B           | Fundamental vs. general survival collapse | Collapsed                     | Maintained distinction       | CRITICAL | RESTORE Exhibit B
  M-4| §5.2 / Indemn.      | Missing "for the avoidance of doubt" retained-liability clause | Absent | Insert clause               | MEDIUM   | ADD

----------------------------------------------------------------------
VIII. RECOMMENDED OVERALL POSITION
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Subject to the two controlling concessions/priorities (concede basket conversion at D-2; treat survival reduction at D-4 as a walk-away), all other counterparty deviations are opposed. Specifically: the indemnification cap reduction (D-1) and the MAE regulatory carve-outs (D-3) are rejected; the retained-liability covenant (D-5) is reinforced; and the missing protections (M-1 through M-4) are to be added. The redline companion (aca-redline.docx) reflects these positions in tracked-changes form.

The primary negotiating red lines are:
  1. Survival period for core representations — WALK-AWAY (D-4 / M-3).
  2. MAE definition — no regulatory-action carve-out (D-3).
  3. Indemnification cap — firm-standard 15% (D-1).

Basket conversion (D-2) is the only permitted concession, per controlling instruction.

Any matter not expressly addressed by this memorandum or the redline, or any new counterparty proposal, should be escalated before concession.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
This memorandum constitutes attorney work product prepared in anticipation of litigation and for settlement/negotiation purposes. Privileged and Confidential.
END OF MEMORANDUM
